models.author_institution: Generic / Textbook Architecture
models.short_description: Simple convolutional network, fast and flexible
models.description: A vanilla convolutional neural network stacking Conv-BN-ReLU blocks with max-pooling for spatial reduction. Originating from LeCun's foundational work on gradient-based learning (1989), this architecture serves as the simplest deep learning baseline. It lacks modern enhancements like skip connections or attention, trading representational power for minimal complexity and fast iteration.
models.best_for: Quick baselines and prototyping across all data types
pros: Extremely fast training and inference
Very low memory footprint
Supports 1D, 2D, and 3D out of the box
Easy to understand and debug
cons: Limited representational capacity for complex tasks
No skip connections — prone to vanishing gradients at depth
Significantly outperformed by modern alternatives

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Kaiming He et al.)
models.short_description: Residual network with skip connections (18 layers)
models.description: ResNet-18 introduced identity shortcut connections that allow gradients to flow directly through the network, solving the degradation problem in deep networks. With 18 layers organized into 4 residual stages using BasicBlock (two 3*3 convolutions per block), it demonstrated that deeper networks could be trained reliably. This landmark 2015 architecture won the ImageNet challenge and remains one of the most widely used backbones in computer vision.
models.best_for: General-purpose feature extraction for medium datasets
pros: Proven reliability across thousands of applications
Skip connections enable stable deep training
Good accuracy-to-compute ratio
Supports all dimensionalities
cons: BasicBlock is less parameter-efficient than Bottleneck
Limited receptive field compared to modern architectures
No attention mechanism for long-range dependencies

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Kaiming He et al.)
models.description: ResNet-34 extends the ResNet family to 34 layers while still using BasicBlock residual units. The additional depth provides greater modeling capacity through more non-linear transformations, enabling the network to learn finer-grained feature hierarchies. It occupies a sweet spot between the lightweight ResNet-18 and the bottleneck-based ResNet-50, offering more capacity without the architectural complexity of 1*1 projection convolutions.
models.best_for: Larger datasets needing more model capacity
pros: More capacity than ResNet-18 with same block type
Straightforward scaling of a proven architecture
Good balance of depth and training speed
Supports all dimensionalities
cons: Nearly double the parameters of ResNet-18
BasicBlock still less efficient than Bottleneck design
Outperformed by modern CNNs at similar compute

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Kaiming He et al.)
models.description: ResNet-50 introduces the Bottleneck block design — a 1*1→3*3→1*1 convolution sequence that reduces and then restores channel dimensions, enabling 50 layers with only slightly more parameters than ResNet-34. This architectural innovation makes deep networks computationally feasible while dramatically increasing representational power. ResNet-50 remains the de facto standard backbone for transfer learning and is one of the most benchmarked models in deep learning history.
models.best_for: Complex feature hierarchies and large-scale tasks
pros: Bottleneck design is highly parameter-efficient
Industry-standard backbone for benchmarking
Excellent feature hierarchies for downstream tasks
Supports all dimensionalities
cons: Heavier than ResNet-18/34 for simple tasks
No modern normalization or attention mechanisms
Receptive field limited by 3*3 kernel stacking

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Kaiming He et al.)
models.description: This variant of ResNet-18 comes pre-initialized with weights learned on the ImageNet-1K dataset (1.28M images, 1000 classes). Transfer learning from these pretrained features dramatically reduces the amount of labeled data needed for new tasks, as the early layers already encode universal visual primitives like edges, textures, and shapes. Fine-tuning is typically done by replacing the classification head and training with a lower learning rate.
models.best_for: 2D image data with limited training samples
pros: Dramatically reduces data requirements via transfer learning
Converges much faster than training from scratch
Proven ImageNet features generalize broadly
Low computational overhead
cons: Restricted to 2D input only
ImageNet biases may not suit all domains
BasicBlock limits capacity for very complex tasks

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Kaiming He et al.)
models.description: ResNet-50 pretrained on ImageNet-1K combines the powerful Bottleneck architecture with rich learned representations. The pretrained features capture complex visual hierarchies from millions of natural images, making it one of the most effective starting points for transfer learning in 2D vision tasks. Its deeper bottleneck structure extracts more discriminative features than ResNet-18, leading to higher accuracy when fine-tuned on downstream tasks.
models.best_for: High-accuracy 2D tasks with transfer learning
pros: Rich pretrained features from deep bottleneck design
Best-in-class transfer learning baseline
Well-supported across all deep learning frameworks
Strong accuracy on diverse 2D domains
cons: Restricted to 2D input only
Larger memory footprint than ResNet-18 pretrained
May be overkill for very simple classification tasks

models.author_institution: Cornell University / Tsinghua University (Gao Huang et al.)
models.short_description: Densely connected network — strong feature reuse
models.description: DenseNet-121 connects each layer to every subsequent layer within a dense block, enabling maximum feature reuse and gradient flow. Unlike ResNets which add skip connections, DenseNet concatenates feature maps, allowing the network to learn compact representations with fewer parameters. Transition layers between dense blocks use 1*1 convolutions and average pooling for dimensionality reduction, making the architecture highly parameter-efficient.
models.best_for: Parameter-efficient training with dense connectivity
pros: Superior parameter efficiency through feature reuse
Strong gradient flow via dense connections
Fewer parameters than ResNets for comparable accuracy
Supports all dimensionalities
cons: High memory consumption due to feature concatenation
Slower inference than ResNets despite fewer parameters
Memory cost grows quadratically with depth

models.author_institution: Cornell University / Tsinghua University (Gao Huang et al.)
models.description: DenseNet-169 extends the DenseNet architecture to 169 layers with more dense blocks and layers per block, providing greater modeling capacity while maintaining the core dense connectivity pattern. The deeper architecture can capture more complex feature interactions through its extended chain of concatenated feature maps. It offers a meaningful step up from DenseNet-121 for tasks where the smaller variant lacks sufficient capacity.
models.best_for: When DenseNet-121 capacity is insufficient
pros: More capacity than DenseNet-121 with same design philosophy
Efficient parameter utilization via dense connections
Stronger feature hierarchies from increased depth
Supports all dimensionalities
cons: Higher memory consumption than DenseNet-121
Feature concatenation memory overhead compounds with depth
Slower training than comparably-sized ResNets

models.author_institution: Cornell University / Tsinghua University (Gao Huang et al.)
models.description: DenseNet-121 pretrained on ImageNet-1K leverages dense connectivity's feature reuse with rich learned visual representations. The densely connected pattern means that pretrained features from all preceding layers are available to every subsequent layer, creating an exceptionally rich feature space for transfer learning. With only 7M parameters, it offers one of the best accuracy-per-parameter ratios among pretrained models.
models.best_for: Efficient transfer learning for 2D image tasks
pros: Excellent accuracy-per-parameter for transfer learning
Rich multi-scale pretrained features via dense connections
Lightweight compared to pretrained ResNet-50
Well-suited for medical imaging and fine-grained tasks
cons: Restricted to 2D input only
Higher memory usage than parameter count suggests
Slower inference than pretrained MobileNets

models.author_institution: Google (Andrew Howard et al.)
models.description: MobileNetV3-Small was designed using a combination of hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) and the NetAdapt algorithm to optimize for mobile CPUs. It employs inverted residual blocks with lightweight depthwise separable convolutions, squeeze-and-excitation attention, and hard-swish activations. This architecture delivers remarkable accuracy for its minuscule parameter count, making it ideal for on-device inference.
models.best_for: Edge deployment, very small 2D datasets, fast inference
pros: Extremely small model size suitable for mobile/edge
Hardware-optimized via NAS
Squeeze-and-excitation provides channel attention
Very fast inference on CPUs and mobile GPUs

2D only — no multi-dimensional support
Accuracy gap compared to larger models

models.author_institution: Google (Andrew Howard et al.)
models.short_description: Efficient mobile architecture with higher capacity
models.description: MobileNetV3-Large scales up the NAS-discovered architecture with wider layers and more inverted residual blocks, providing significantly better accuracy while maintaining mobile-friendly inference speeds. It incorporates h-swish activations in later layers and squeeze-and-excitation modules for channel recalibration. The architecture strikes an optimal balance between accuracy and latency for mobile deployment scenarios.
models.best_for: Mobile deployment with better accuracy than Small variant
pros: Strong accuracy for a mobile-class model
Well-optimized for mobile GPU and CPU inference
Pretrained ImageNet weights available
Good accuracy-latency trade-off

2D only — no multi-dimensional support

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.short_description: Compound-scaled CNN — balanced width, depth, resolution
models.description: EfficientNet-B0 is the baseline model discovered by neural architecture search that introduced compound scaling — simultaneously scaling network width, depth, and input resolution using fixed ratios. Built on mobile inverted bottleneck convolution (MBConv) blocks with squeeze-and-excitation, it achieved state-of-the-art accuracy with 8.4* fewer parameters than previous best models. This 2019 architecture fundamentally changed how the community thinks about model scaling.
models.best_for: Small-to-medium 2D datasets with efficient compute
pros: Excellent accuracy-per-FLOP through compound scaling
Foundational NAS-discovered architecture
Squeeze-and-excitation enhances channel attention
Lightweight enough for consumer GPUs
cons: Training can be slower due to SE blocks and swish
2D only — no multi-dimensional support
Superseded by EfficientNetV2 for training speed

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.description: EfficientNet-B2 applies the compound scaling coefficients to uniformly increase width, depth, and resolution from the B0 baseline. With approximately 1.7* more parameters than B0, it processes larger input resolutions (260*260 vs 224*224) and uses wider/deeper MBConv blocks. This balanced scaling provides meaningfully better accuracy while maintaining the efficiency principles of the EfficientNet family.
models.best_for: Medium 2D datasets needing more expressiveness
pros: Balanced scaling provides smooth accuracy improvement
Still relatively lightweight and efficient
Higher resolution input captures finer details
Good middle-ground in the EfficientNet family
cons: Higher memory usage than B0 due to larger resolution
2D only
Training slower than comparably-sized ConvNeXt models

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.description: EfficientNet-B4 scales the architecture further with 380*380 input resolution, providing significantly higher accuracy at the cost of increased compute. It represents the point in the EfficientNet family where accuracy begins to rival much larger models like ResNet-152, while using far fewer parameters. The compound scaling ensures that the increased capacity is distributed evenly across width, depth, and resolution dimensions.

pros: High accuracy rivaling much larger models
Efficient parameter utilization via compound scaling
Large input resolution for fine-grained recognition
Strong pretrained features for transfer learning

2D only
Training time increases substantially with resolution

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.description: EfficientNet-B7 pushes compound scaling to its practical limit with 600*600 input resolution, 66M parameters, and the deepest/widest MBConv configuration. It achieved 84.3% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet — state-of-the-art at its release — while being 8.4* smaller than the previous best GPipe model. However, the extreme resolution and depth make it one of the most resource-demanding models in the EfficientNet family.

State-of-the-art ImageNet accuracy at release

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.short_description: Progressive learning + fused MBConv for faster training
models.description: EfficientNetV2-S introduces Fused-MBConv blocks that replace the depthwise+pointwise pattern with a single fused convolution in early stages, dramatically improving training speed on modern accelerators. Combined with progressive learning — gradually increasing image resolution and regularization during training — it trains 5-11* faster than EfficientNetV1 while achieving better accuracy. This 2021 architecture represents a significant evolution in efficient model design.

pros: 5-11* faster training than EfficientNetV1
Fused-MBConv improves hardware utilization
Progressive learning improves regularization
Better accuracy than V1 with faster convergence

Fused convolutions increase early-stage compute

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.description: EfficientNetV2-M scales up the V2 architecture with more Fused-MBConv and MBConv blocks, providing substantially higher accuracy while retaining the training speed advantages of progressive learning. It uses a mix of fused convolutions in early stages and depthwise separable convolutions in later stages, optimizing for both training throughput and model quality. This mid-range variant offers an excellent trade-off for serious production workloads.

models.author_institution: Google (Mingxing Tan & Quoc V. Le)
models.description: EfficientNetV2-L is the largest variant in the V2 family, pushing the Fused-MBConv architecture to maximum scale with 117M parameters. Despite its size, it trains significantly faster than comparably accurate models from the V1 family due to progressive learning and optimized block design. It achieves near state-of-the-art ImageNet accuracy while maintaining the efficiency principles that define the EfficientNet lineage.

models.author_institution: Facebook AI Research (Ilija Radosavovic et al.)
models.description: RegNet-Y 400MF belongs to the RegNet design space — a family of networks discovered by systematically exploring network width, depth, and group width patterns. The 'Y' variant adds squeeze-and-excitation modules for channel attention. Operating at a 400M FLOPs budget, it delivers strong accuracy for its compute class. The RegNet philosophy emphasizes simple, regular network structures that scale predictably, discovered through population-level analysis of network design spaces.

Squeeze-and-excitation adds channel attention
Simple, regular structure is hardware-friendly

models.author_institution: Facebook AI Research (Ilija Radosavovic et al.)
models.description: RegNet-Y 800MF doubles the compute budget of the 400MF variant, providing wider layers and more groups for increased representational capacity. The design space methodology ensures that this scaling is optimal — each additional FLOP is allocated to maximize accuracy. With squeeze-and-excitation attention and well-tuned group convolutions, it represents one of the most efficient models at its compute level.

models.description: RegNet-Y 1.6GF operates at a mid-range compute budget, providing substantial modeling capacity with predictable performance characteristics. The regular network structure — with linearly increasing widths and constant group widths — makes it particularly well-suited for hardware optimization and batch inference. At 10.3M parameters, it offers a compelling alternative to EfficientNet-B0/B2 with more predictable latency profiles.

models.author_institution: Facebook AI Research (Ilija Radosavovic et al.)
models.description: RegNet-Y 3.2GF scales into the higher-compute regime with 17.9M parameters, providing strong feature extraction capabilities for demanding 2D tasks. The systematic design space approach ensures that the architecture avoids common scaling pitfalls — each stage's width and depth are optimally balanced. Combined with SE attention, it delivers competitive accuracy against hand-designed architectures like ResNet-50 at a similar compute budget.

At this scale, it competes directly with large ConvNets and even some Transformer-based models in terms of accuracy. The regular structure and group convolutions enable efficient distributed training, while the 8GF compute budget allows for rich, deep feature hierarchies suitable for large-scale visual recognition tasks.

models.author_institution: Meta AI Research (Zhuang Liu et al.)
models.description: ConvNeXt systematically modernizes a standard ResNet by adopting Transformer design principles: patchify stem, inverted bottleneck blocks, depthwise separable 7*7 convolutions, fewer activation functions, LayerNorm instead of BatchNorm, and GELU activations. This 2022 architecture from Meta AI demonstrated that pure convolutional networks can match or exceed Swin Transformer accuracy when trained with modern recipes, challenging the assumed superiority of attention-based models.

models.description: ConvNeXt Small widens the channel dimensions across all four stages compared to the Tiny variant, providing greater modeling capacity while maintaining the same modernized ConvNet design philosophy. The increased width allows for richer feature representations at each spatial resolution, making it better suited for datasets with higher visual complexity or fine-grained distinctions.

models.short_description: ConvNeXt V2 with Global Response Normalization
models.description: ConvNeXt V2 enhances the original ConvNeXt with Global Response Normalization (GRN) — a novel layer that addresses feature collapse in self-supervised learning by normalizing and calibrating channel responses based on their global statistics. Co-designed with the Fully Convolutional Masked Autoencoder (FCMAE) pretraining framework, V2 models achieve significantly better representations especially when pretrained with self-supervised objectives, closing the gap between ConvNets and masked-image-modeling ViTs.

models.author_institution: Tsinghua University / MEGVII (Xiaohan Ding et al.)
models.description: UniRepLKNet pushes convolutional kernel sizes to extremes (up to 31*31 or larger) using structural reparameterization, enabling convolutions to capture very long-range dependencies traditionally reserved for attention mechanisms. The architecture uses dilated reparam blocks that decompose large kernels into efficient parallel branches during training, then merge them into a single large kernel for inference. This provides Transformer-like global receptive fields with CNN computational characteristics.

models.short_description: Compact Vision Transformer with patch embeddings
models.description: ViT Tiny is a compact variant of the Vision Transformer that splits input images into fixed-size patches, linearly embeds them, and processes the sequence with standard Transformer encoder blocks featuring multi-head self-attention (MHSA). Introduced by Google Brain in 2020, ViT demonstrated that pure Transformer architectures — originally designed for NLP — can achieve excellent results on image classification when trained on sufficient data, challenging the dominance of CNNs.

Each layer applies multi-head self-attention followed by an MLP block with GELU activation and LayerNorm. This mid-range configuration captures complex token interactions while remaining trainable on single-GPU setups with moderate dataset sizes.

The global self-attention at every layer enables the model to learn dynamic, input-dependent feature aggregation patterns that are impossible for fixed-kernel convolutions.

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Ze Liu et al.)
models.description: Swin Transformer revolutionized vision Transformers by introducing shifted-window (Swin) self-attention, which computes attention within local windows and shifts them between layers to enable cross-window connections. This achieves linear computational complexity with respect to image size (vs. quadratic for ViT) while maintaining a hierarchical feature pyramid similar to CNNs. The 2021 architecture won the ICCV Best Paper Honorable Mention and became a dominant backbone for detection and segmentation.

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Ze Liu et al.)
models.short_description: Larger Swin Transformer with more capacity
models.description: Swin Small doubles the depth of the third stage compared to Swin Tiny, significantly increasing the model's capacity for learning complex visual patterns at the 1/16 resolution level. With 48.8M parameters, it provides a meaningful accuracy boost while retaining the efficient shifted-window attention mechanism. This variant is well-suited for tasks requiring richer mid-level feature representations.
models.best_for: Medium-to-large 2D datasets with complex patterns
pros: Deeper third stage for richer mid-level features
Efficient shifted-window attention scales well
Strong pretrained features for transfer learning
Excellent for detection and segmentation tasks
cons: 2D only
Higher memory than Swin Tiny
Fixed window size limits adaptability

models.author_institution: Microsoft Research (Ze Liu et al.)
models.description: Swin Base is the largest standard Swin variant with 86.7M parameters and 128-dimensional initial embeddings, providing maximum capacity within the Swin architecture family. Its hierarchical four-stage design with progressive downsampling generates rich multi-scale feature maps. Combined with shifted-window attention's linear complexity, it can process high-resolution images efficiently while capturing both local details and global context through cross-window interactions.
models.best_for: Large 2D datasets with hierarchical features
pros: Maximum capacity in the Swin family
Multi-scale features for dense prediction tasks
Linear complexity enables practical high-resolution processing
State-of-the-art pretrained features
cons: High GPU memory requirements
2D only
Complex shifted-window implementation

models.author_institution: Google Research (Zhengzhong Tu et al.)
models.short_description: Multi-axis attention with blocked local + dilated global
models.description: MaxViT introduces a novel multi-axis attention mechanism that combines blocked local attention (within spatial windows) and dilated global attention (across a grid of sparsely sampled tokens) in alternating layers. This dual-attention design captures both fine-grained local patterns and long-range global dependencies with linear complexity. Each MaxViT block also includes MBConv layers, creating a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture that benefits from both convolutional inductive biases and global attention.
models.best_for: 2D tasks needing both local and global attention
pros: Captures both local and global dependencies efficiently
Linear complexity via blocked + dilated attention
Hybrid MBConv+attention design leverages best of both worlds
Strong across classification, detection, and generation
cons: 2D only
Complex multi-axis attention implementation
Less widely adopted than Swin Transformer

models.author_institution: Google Research (Zhengzhong Tu et al.)
models.description: MaxViT Small increases the channel dimensions and block counts compared to MaxViT Tiny, providing greater capacity for learning complex multi-scale visual features. The expanded multi-axis attention mechanism can capture more diverse spatial relationships, while the increased MBConv capacity enriches local feature extraction. This variant targets tasks demanding higher accuracy with complex spatial dependencies.
models.best_for: Complex 2D tasks with multi-scale feature needs
pros: Enhanced multi-axis attention for complex patterns
Stronger local+global feature integration
Good scaling from Tiny variant
Hybrid architecture benefits from both paradigms
cons: Significant GPU memory requirements
2D only
Training complexity due to multi-axis attention

models.author_institution: Google Research (Zhengzhong Tu et al.)
models.description: MaxViT Base is the largest variant at 119.1M parameters, maximizing the multi-axis attention mechanism's capacity. At this scale, the combination of blocked local attention, dilated global attention, and MBConv layers creates one of the most expressive vision architectures available. It has shown particularly strong results on image generation tasks (as a backbone for diffusion models) in addition to standard classification and detection benchmarks.
models.best_for: Large 2D datasets with ample GPU resources
pros: Maximum multi-axis attention capacity
State-of-the-art on multiple vision benchmarks
Excellent backbone for generative models
Comprehensive local+global feature modeling
cons: Very high compute and memory requirements
2D only
Complex architecture — harder to debug and customize

models.author_institution: Apple (Pavan Kumar Anasosalu Vasu et al.)
models.description: FastViT-T8 introduces RepMixer — a reparameterizable token mixing layer that uses depthwise convolutions during training and merges them into a single efficient operation at inference. Combined with a hybrid architecture that uses convolutional stages early and attention stages later, FastViT achieves a remarkable latency-accuracy trade-off. Developed by Apple for on-device deployment, it is one of the fastest hybrid vision models available.
models.best_for: Real-time 2D inference with minimal resources
pros: Extremely fast inference via structural reparameterization
Excellent latency-accuracy trade-off
Designed for on-device and real-time deployment
RepMixer is highly hardware-efficient

Limited capacity for complex visual tasks
Niche — less community support than mainstream models

models.author_institution: Apple (Pavan Kumar Anasosalu Vasu et al.)
models.short_description: Fast hybrid with slightly more capacity
models.description: FastViT-T12 increases model capacity over T8 with wider channels and more RepMixer blocks, providing better accuracy while retaining the ultra-fast inference characteristics of the FastViT family. The additional capacity enables it to capture more complex visual patterns, making it suitable for applications where T8's accuracy is slightly insufficient but real-time speed is still critical.
models.best_for: Speed-critical 2D tasks with better accuracy
pros: Better accuracy than T8 with similar speed profile
RepMixer enables efficient inference
Good for edge deployment requiring moderate accuracy
Apple-optimized for mobile hardware

models.short_description: Small FastViT balancing speed and accuracy
models.description: FastViT-S12 moves into the 'Small' model tier with 8.8M parameters, using wider channels than the T-series while maintaining RepMixer's efficient token mixing. This variant balances inference speed and modeling capacity, making it practical for production deployments where both latency and accuracy requirements are moderate. The hybrid CNN-attention design captures local patterns via convolutions and global relationships via later attention stages.

models.author_institution: Apple (Pavan Kumar Anasosalu Vasu et al.)
models.description: FastViT-SA12 adds explicit self-attention (SA) stages on top of the RepMixer token mixing, creating a more expressive model that can capture complex global interactions. The 'SA' suffix indicates additional attention blocks in the later network stages, providing a meaningful accuracy boost over the S12 variant at a moderate latency cost. This design is optimal when slightly more compute budget is available for improved feature quality.

models.author_institution: Sea AI Lab / NUS (Weihao Yu et al.)
models.short_description: MetaFormer with separable attention and convolutions
models.description: CAFormer (Convolution-Attention Former) is built on the MetaFormer hypothesis — that the general Transformer architecture is more important than the specific token mixer. It uses depthwise separable convolutions in early stages for local feature extraction and vanilla self-attention in later stages for global reasoning. This principled hybrid design, validated by the MetaFormer framework from Sea AI Lab, achieves excellent accuracy by leveraging the right inductive bias at each spatial resolution.
models.best_for: 2D tasks needing strong token mixing strategies
pros: Principled design based on MetaFormer framework
Optimal token mixer at each resolution stage
Strong accuracy-compute trade-off
Well-validated architecture design methodology

Less mainstream than Swin or ConvNeXt

models.author_institution: Sea AI Lab / NUS (Weihao Yu et al.)
models.description: CAFormer-S36 doubles the depth of the S18 variant to 36 blocks, providing significantly more layers for both convolutional and attention-based token mixing. The increased depth enables the model to learn more complex feature transformations and more nuanced attention patterns in the later stages. This deeper variant excels on tasks requiring fine-grained distinctions or complex spatial reasoning.

models.author_institution: Sea AI Lab / NUS (Weihao Yu et al.)
models.description: CAFormer-M36 combines the 36-block depth with wider channel dimensions ('Medium' width), creating the most capable CAFormer variant in this collection. The expanded width provides richer feature representations at every stage, while the depth enables complex multi-step reasoning. This variant demonstrates the MetaFormer design's capacity to scale effectively along both width and depth dimensions.
models.best_for: High-capacity 2D feature extraction
pros: Maximum capacity in the CAFormer family
Rich features from combined depth and width scaling

models.author_institution: Sea AI Lab / NUS (Weihao Yu et al.)
models.short_description: MetaFormer using pooling instead of attention
models.description: PoolFormer is the groundbreaking architecture that validated the MetaFormer hypothesis by replacing the attention mechanism with a simple average pooling operation as the token mixer — and still achieving competitive accuracy. This 2021 experiment proved that the general Transformer-style architecture (norm → mixer → norm → MLP) is more important than the specific mixing mechanism. Despite using no learned parameters in its token mixer, PoolFormer-S12 achieves accuracy comparable to DeiT-Small.

Extremely simple and efficient token mixing
No learned parameters in the mixing operation

models.author_institution: MIT (Han Cai et al.)
models.description: EfficientViT-M1 replaces the quadratic softmax attention with a linear attention mechanism (ReLU-based kernel approximation), reducing both memory usage and computation to linear complexity in sequence length. Developed at MIT, this architecture is specifically designed for deployment on memory-constrained devices. The lightweight design uses a cascaded group attention pattern that reduces redundancy across attention heads, maximizing performance per parameter.
models.best_for: Ultra-lightweight 2D inference on limited hardware
pros: Linear attention complexity reduces memory dramatically
Cascaded group attention eliminates head redundancy
Extremely small model suitable for microcontrollers
Efficient inference on CPU and edge devices
cons: 2D only
Linear attention approximation loses some expressiveness
Very limited capacity for complex tasks

models.author_institution: MIT (Han Cai et al.)
models.description: EfficientViT-B1 scales up from the M-series with a balanced architecture that uses cascaded group attention to efficiently mix tokens across spatial dimensions. The B-series introduces wider channels and more stages while maintaining the linear-complexity attention mechanism. This variant provides a strong accuracy-speed trade-off suitable for edge GPUs and mobile devices that can handle slightly larger models than the M-series.
models.best_for: Efficient 2D tasks with good accuracy-speed trade-off
pros: Strong accuracy-latency balance
Linear attention scales to higher resolutions

models.author_institution: MIT (Han Cai et al.)
models.description: EfficientViT-B2 further expands the B-series with wider channels and deeper stages, pushing the accuracy boundary while retaining linear-complexity attention. At 21.8M parameters, it enters the mid-range model category and competes with standard ViT-Small and EfficientNet-B2 while offering superior inference speed due to its efficient attention mechanism. The architecture demonstrates that linear attention can scale to meaningful model sizes without sacrificing quality.

models.short_description: Large EfficientViT — high accuracy, efficient inference
models.description: EfficientViT-L2 is the largest variant in the MIT EfficientViT family, pushing linear attention to 60.5M parameters. At this scale, the architecture achieves accuracy competitive with standard quadratic-attention Transformers while maintaining significantly faster inference throughput. The L-series introduces additional architectural optimizations for large-scale deployment, making it suitable for server-side inference where throughput at moderate latency is the primary concern.

models.author_institution: Carnegie Mellon / Princeton (Albert Gu & Tri Dao)
models.short_description: Selective state space model for 1D sequences
models.description: Mamba introduces selective state spaces — a groundbreaking evolution of structured SSMs where the state transition matrices are input-dependent, allowing the model to selectively focus on or ignore information along the sequence. Combined with a hardware-aware parallel scan algorithm, Mamba achieves linear-time sequence processing with the expressiveness of attention-like mechanisms. This 2023 architecture has rapidly become the leading alternative to Transformers for long-sequence modeling.

models.author_institution: Stanford / Carnegie Mellon (Albert Gu et al.)
models.short_description: Compact diagonal structured state space model
models.description: S4D (Structured State Space for Sequences — Diagonal) simplifies the original S4 model by using diagonal state matrices instead of the full HiPPO-initialized DPLR matrices. This diagonal parameterization is mathematically equivalent for many practical cases while being significantly simpler to implement and faster to compute. At only 0.8M parameters, S4D Small is one of the smallest models capable of capturing very long-range dependencies in sequential data.

Simplified diagonal parameterization is easy to implement

models.author_institution: Stanford / Carnegie Mellon (Albert Gu et al.)
models.description: S4D is the standard-sized diagonal state space model that models sequential data through continuous-time linear recurrences discretized for digital processing. The diagonal state matrix enables efficient parallel computation via convolution in training mode and recurrent processing at inference. S4D captures dependencies across thousands of time steps, making it particularly effective for audio, scientific signals, and other long-range sequential tasks.
models.best_for: Long-range 1D dependencies at sub-quadratic cost

Dual computation modes: convolution (train) and recurrence (infer)

models.short_description: Large S4D with expanded state dimensions

The larger state space enables more nuanced representations of sequential dynamics, while the increased channel width allows for richer feature extraction at each time step. This variant targets challenging 1D tasks where the standard S4D's capacity is insufficient.

models.author_institution: Huazhong UST / Horizon Robotics (Lianghui Zhu et al.)
models.description: Vision Mamba (Vim) adapts the selective state space model to 2D vision by flattening image patches into sequences and processing them with bidirectional Mamba blocks. The bidirectional scanning — processing patches left-to-right and right-to-left — enables the model to capture spatial relationships in both directions, partially compensating for the loss of 2D spatial structure. Vim achieves competitive accuracy with ViT while scaling linearly with image resolution instead of quadratically.

The increased model size enables richer bidirectional scanning patterns and more expressive state dynamics. At 51.1M parameters, it competes with ViT-Small and Swin-Tiny while offering better scaling to high-resolution inputs.

The massive state space and wide channels enable the model to learn extremely rich bidirectional representations through selective state transitions. While resource-intensive, it demonstrates the potential of SSM architectures to scale to large vision models, offering a fundamentally different computational paradigm from Transformer-based vision.

models.author_institution: CMU (Shaojie Bai, J. Zico Kolter, Vladlen Koltun)
models.description: TCN Small is a compact temporal convolutional network that uses causal dilated convolutions — convolutions that exponentially increase their dilation factor at each layer to create an exponentially growing receptive field. Combined with residual connections and weight normalization, TCNs demonstrated in 2018 that convolutional architectures could match or exceed RNN/LSTM performance on sequence modeling benchmarks while being more parallelizable and having more stable gradients.

models.description: The standard TCN uses multiple residual blocks of causal dilated 1D convolutions with exponentially increasing dilation factors (1, 2, 4, 8, ...), creating a large effective receptive field while maintaining a manageable parameter count. Each block includes weight normalization, ReLU activation, and dropout for regularization. This architecture provides a strong general-purpose baseline for 1D time series regression and classification tasks.

The wider dilated convolutions capture more complex temporal patterns at each dilation scale, while additional blocks extend the maximum receptive field. This variant is designed for challenging temporal tasks with complex, long-range dependencies.

models.author_institution: DeepMind (Aäron van den Oord et al.)
models.description: WaveNet Small is a compact version of DeepMind's WaveNet architecture that uses gated dilated causal convolutions — splitting each layer's output into tanh (filter) and sigmoid (gate) branches that are element-wise multiplied. This gating mechanism, inspired by LSTM gates, allows the network to learn which temporal features to pass through. Originally designed for raw audio waveform generation, the architecture excels on any 1D signal processing task.

models.author_institution: DeepMind (Aäron van den Oord et al.)
models.short_description: Gated dilated convolutions for sequence modeling
models.description: WaveNet uses stacked gated dilated causal convolutions with skip connections that sum outputs from all layers, creating a rich multi-resolution temporal representation. The doubling dilation pattern (1, 2, 4, ..., 512) across multiple stacks creates an exponentially large receptive field capable of modeling thousands of time steps. Originally achieving state-of-the-art text-to-speech quality in 2016, WaveNet's architecture has proven effective for general 1D temporal regression and signal processing.

models.short_description: Large WaveNet with deeper dilation stacks

The deeper stacking of gated dilated convolutions enables the model to process very long waveforms with multiple overlapping receptive field patterns. This variant is suited for tasks requiring the widest possible temporal context in 1D data.

models.author_institution: Facebook AI Research (Du Tran et al.)
models.short_description: ResNet with 3D convolutions for volumetric data
models.description: 3D ResNet-18 extends the ResNet architecture by replacing all 2D convolutions with 3D convolutions, enabling it to process volumetric data (depth * height * width) natively. Each 3D convolutional kernel operates across all three spatial dimensions simultaneously, capturing patterns that span the full volume. Originally developed for video understanding (treating time as the third dimension), it is equally applicable to medical imaging (CT/MRI), scientific simulations, and other volumetric datasets.

ResNet skip connections work well in 3D

models.author_institution: Facebook AI Research (Du Tran et al.)
models.description: MC3-18 (Mixed Convolution 3D) uses 3D convolutions in early layers to capture low-level spatiotemporal features and transitions to 2D convolutions in later layers for efficient high-level feature extraction. This mixed approach, introduced alongside R(2+1)D by Facebook AI, significantly reduces computation compared to full 3D convolutions while retaining most of the representational benefit. The insight is that temporal and spatial features can be effectively factorized at deeper layers.

models.author_institution: University of Freiburg (Olaf Ronneberger et al.)
models.description: U-Net features a symmetric encoder-decoder architecture connected by skip connections at each resolution level, enabling precise localization by combining deep semantic features with shallow spatial details. Originally designed for biomedical image segmentation (2015), this regression variant replaces the classification head with continuous output, making it suitable for dense prediction tasks like depth estimation, super-resolution, and field regression. The skip connections are the key innovation, allowing the decoder to recover fine spatial details lost during encoding.

models.author_institution: University of Freiburg (Olaf Ronneberger et al.)
models.short_description: U-shaped encoder-decoder for dense 2D field regression
models.description: U-Net Field keeps the decoder's spatial tensor and projects it to the target channels with a 1x1 convolution, predicting a full property map rather than a vector. Skip connections at every resolution level combine deep context with fine spatial detail, and the prediction is interpolated when the target grid differs from the input grid. WaveDL routes dense (N,H,W) or (N,C,H,W) targets to this model, making it suited to field reconstruction tasks such as seismic imaging and elastography.
